title: A Teaspoon of Soil Holds More Life Than There Are People on Earth

scenes.text: A teaspoon of soil holds more living things than people on Earth.
There are about eight billion of us. One gram of healthy soil can hold around a billion bacteria.
A teaspoon is about five grams. That's billions of bacteria, plus tens of millions of fungi, plus mites, worms and creatures with no common name.
Those fungi grow as fine white threads that carry water and nutrients to plant roots, like an underground delivery network.
That crowd exists because dead leaves, roots and animals are food, and billions of tiny mouths are breaking them down right now.
That's why gardeners say feed the soil, not the plant. Every tomato you've ever eaten was built by that invisible crowd. What's growing in your garden?

description:
A teaspoon of soil holds more living things than there are people on Earth.
USDA soil scientists put the number of bacteria at around one billion per gram of soil, with another 10 to 20 million fungi, so a five-gram teaspoon easily outnumbers the eight billion people on the planet. Soil conservation guides use the same comparison: a lump of healthy soil the size of your big toe contains more organisms than there are people on Earth.
What's growing in your garden?
